source.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Another parable he set before them saying, Has been likened the kingdom of the heavens to a man having sown good seed in the field of him.

en.L: He put another parable before them, saying, "The kingdom of the heavens has been compared to a man who sowed good seed in his field.
en.B: Then Jesus set another parable before them: "The kingdom of heaven is like the story of a man who sowed good seed in his field.
en.R: Then Jesus told them another parable. He said, "The kingdom of heaven is like what happened when a man planted good seed in his field.

es.L: Otra parábola les presentó, diciendo: «El reino de los cielos ha sido comparado a un hombre que había sembrado semilla buena en su campo.
es.B: Luego Jesús les presentó otra parábola: «Con el reino de los cielos pasa como con un hombre que sembró buena semilla en su campo.
es.R: Después Jesús les contó otra parábola. Les dijo: «El reino de los cielos es como lo que pasó cuando un hombre sembró buena semilla en su campo.

sw.L: Aliwawekea mfano mwingine, akisema, "Ufalme wa mbinguni umefananishwa na mtu aliyekuwa amepanda mbegu nzuri shambani mwake.
sw.B: Kisha Yesu aliwaletea mfano mwingine: "Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama habari ya mtu aliyepanda mbegu nzuri shambani mwake.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwaambia mfano mwingine. Akasema, "Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama jambo lililotokea mtu mmoja alipopanda mbegu nzuri shambani mwake.

decisions.choice: has been compared: the kingdom is like the whole story that follows
alternatives: the kingdom is like the man
decisions.reason: The verb is a past passive, "has been made like". The comparison is with what happens in the story, not with the man alone.

decisions.choice: put before: set out for them to consider
decisions.reason: The verb is used of setting food before guests and of setting out teaching.

decisions.choice: like the story of a man (B); like what happened when a man (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the comparison is with the whole story. The man who sows is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos (every level)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering for Matthew, recorded once in this passage. The plural keeps Matthew's way of speaking of God's kingdom without naming God, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: parábola (every level); Con el reino de los cielos pasa como con... (B)
decisions.reason: "Parábola" is the term-sheet word, recorded once in this passage. Balanced says that the kingdom is like the whole story, not like the man alone (meaning decision m1), with an ordinary Spanish turn of phrase, as the English "like the story of" does.

decisions.choice: mfano; ufalme wa mbinguni (every level)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet words for Matthew, recorded once in this passage. "Mfano" is a comparison or picture-story; "ufalme wa mbinguni" keeps Matthew's way of speaking of God's kingdom without naming God.

source.text: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν.

records.literal_gloss: In but the sleeping the men came of him the enemy and sowed over weeds in the middle of the wheat and went away.

en.L: But while {{gender:people|men}} were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away.
en.B: But while people slept, an enemy of his came and scattered weeds all through the wheat, then went off.
en.R: But one night, while everyone was asleep, the man's enemy came. He planted weeds among the wheat and then left.

es.L: Pero mientras {{gender:la gente dormía|los hombres dormían}}, vino su enemigo y sembró encima cizaña en medio del trigo, y se fue.
es.B: Pero mientras todos dormían, vino un enemigo suyo, esparció cizaña por todo el trigal y se marchó.
es.R: Pero una noche, mientras todos dormían, llegó el enemigo de aquel hombre. Sembró mala hierba entre el trigo y se fue.

sw.L: Lakini watu walipokuwa usingizini, adui yake alikuja akaongeza kupanda magugu katikati ya ngano, kisha akaondoka.
sw.B: Lakini watu walipokuwa wamelala, adui yake mmoja alikuja, akatawanya magugu kila mahali katikati ya ngano, kisha akaenda zake.
sw.R: Lakini usiku mmoja, kila mtu alipokuwa amelala, adui wa mtu huyo alikuja. Akapanda magugu katikati ya ngano, kisha akaondoka.

decisions.choice: weeds: darnel, a weedy grass that looks like wheat until it forms heads
decisions.reason: The word names a grass of grain fields whose seeds are bitter and can make people ill. While young it is hard to tell from wheat (13:26).

decisions.choice: the enemy sowed weeds: a known act of spite against a farmer
decisions.reason: Sowing weeds in someone's field was a way to ruin a harvest. Roman law later dealt with this kind of damage.

decisions.choice: while people were sleeping: at night, when no one would see
decisions.reason: The phrase sets the time. It does not blame the man's workers.

decisions.choice: weeds
decisions.reason: "Darnel" is a rare word and "tares" an old one. All levels say "weeds" and the meaning note names the plant.

decisions.choice: one night
decisions.reason: Readable says when people slept.

decisions.choice: cizaña (L, B); mala hierba (R)
decisions.reason: "Cizaña" is the Spanish name of darnel, the grass of meaning decision m1 that looks like wheat until it forms heads. Readable says "mala hierba", as the English says "weeds".

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente dormía|los hombres dormían}} (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: Spanish has the same two wordings for the Greek's general "the men"; the verb changes with the noun, so the span takes it in.

decisions.choice: magugu (every level)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no everyday name for darnel, the grass of meaning decision m1; "magugu" (weeds) is the plain word, as the English says "weeds". "Watu" needs no gender span.

source.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν, τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια.

records.literal_gloss: When but sprouted the grass and fruit produced, then appeared also the weeds.

en.L: And when the plants sprouted and produced grain, then the weeds also appeared.
en.B: When the wheat came up and began to form heads of grain, the weeds showed up as well.
en.R: The wheat grew and made heads of grain. Then everyone could see the weeds too.

es.L: Y cuando la planta brotó y produjo grano, entonces se hizo visible también la cizaña.
es.B: Cuando el trigo creció y comenzó a echar espigas, también apareció la cizaña.
es.R: El trigo creció y echó espigas. Entonces todos pudieron ver también la mala hierba.

sw.L: Na majani yalipochipuka na kutoa nafaka, wakati huo magugu pia yalionekana.
sw.B: Ngano ilipoota na kuanza kutoa masuke, magugu nayo yalijitokeza.
sw.R: Ngano ilikua, ikatoa masuke. Kisha kila mtu aliweza kuyaona magugu pia.

decisions.choice: then the weeds appeared: only when the grain formed could the darnel be told apart
decisions.reason: The weeds were there from the start, but they looked like wheat until the heads formed.

decisions.choice: the plants: the green blades of grain
decisions.reason: The word means grass or green plants. Here it is the young wheat.

source.text: προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ· Κύριε, οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ;

records.literal_gloss: Having come but the slaves of the master of the house said to him, Lord, not good seed did you sow in your field?

en.L: And the slaves of the householder came and said to him, 'Master, did you not sow good seed in your field?
en.B: The landowner's servants came to him and said, 'Master, surely it was good seed you sowed in your field?
en.R: The owner's servants came to him. They said, 'Master, you planted good seed in your field, did you not?

es.L: Y acercándose los esclavos del dueño de casa, le dijeron: “Señor, ¿no sembraste en tu campo semilla buena?
es.B: Los siervos del propietario fueron a decirle: “Señor, ¿no era buena la semilla que sembraste en tu campo?
es.R: Los siervos del dueño fueron a hablar con él. Le dijeron: “Señor, tú sembraste buena semilla en tu campo, ¿verdad?

sw.L: Na watumwa wa mwenye nyumba wakamjia, wakamwambia, 'Bwana, je, si mbegu nzuri uliyoipanda katika shamba lako?
sw.B: Watumishi wa mwenye shamba walimwendea, wakamwambia, 'Bwana, bila shaka ulipanda mbegu nzuri shambani mwako, sivyo?
sw.R: Watumishi wa mwenye shamba walimjia, wakasema, 'Bwana, ulipanda mbegu nzuri shambani mwako, sivyo?

decisions.choice: slaves: servants owned by the householder
decisions.reason: The word means slaves, as at 8:9 and 10:24-25. Large households had slaves who worked the land.

decisions.choice: Master: a respectful address to the owner
alternatives: Lord, as an address to God
decisions.reason: The word means lord or master. In the story it is the slaves' address to their owner.

decisions.choice: did you not sow good seed?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The slaves are sure the seed was good and so cannot explain the weeds.

decisions.choice: Master
decisions.reason: The slaves speak to their owner, so all levels say "Master". The householder is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15.

decisions.choice: landowner (B); owner (R); householder (L)
decisions.reason: He owns the house and the field.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavos (L); siervos (B, R); Señor
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering of the Greek word for slave, recorded once in this passage: Literal says what they were (meaning decision m1), Balanced and Readable the ordinary word for a master's workers. "Señor" is the polite address to the owner (meaning decision m2), capitalised only because it begins the speech.

decisions.choice: watumwa (L); watumishi (B, R); mwenye nyumba (L); mwenye shamba (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering of the Greek word for slave, recorded once in this passage: Literal says what they were (meaning decision m1), Balanced and Readable the ordinary word for a master's workers. Balanced and Readable call the householder "mwenye shamba", since the story is about his field.

source.text: πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια;

records.literal_gloss: From where then has it weeds?

en.L: Where then does it get weeds?'
en.B: So where have these weeds come from?'
en.R: So where did all these weeds come from?'

es.L: ¿De dónde, pues, tiene cizaña?”.
es.B: ¿De dónde ha salido, entonces, esta cizaña?”.
es.R: ¿De dónde salió entonces toda esta mala hierba?”.

sw.L: Basi, linayapata wapi magugu?'
sw.B: Basi magugu haya yametoka wapi?'
sw.R: Basi magugu haya yote yametoka wapi?'

decisions.choice: where then: the slaves cannot account for the weeds
decisions.reason: "Then" draws the conclusion: if the seed was good, the weeds came from somewhere else.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐποίησεν.

records.literal_gloss: He but said to them, Enemy a man this did.

en.L: And he said to them, 'A man [who is] an enemy did this.'
en.B: 'An enemy has done this,' he told them.
en.R: He answered, 'Someone who hates me did this.'

es.L: Y él les dijo: “Un hombre enemigo ha hecho esto”.
es.B: “Esto lo ha hecho un enemigo”, les dijo.
es.R: Él les respondió: “Esto lo hizo alguien que me odia”.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, 'Mtu adui amefanya hivi.'
sw.B: Akawaambia, 'Adui fulani amefanya jambo hili.'
sw.R: Akajibu, 'Mtu anayenichukia ndiye aliyefanya hivi.'

decisions.choice: an enemy, a man: some enemy, a hostile person
alternatives: a man who is my enemy, named
decisions.reason: The two nouns together mean "an enemy". The owner knows it was done on purpose.

decisions.choice: Someone who hates me
decisions.reason: Readable says what an enemy is.

source.text: οἱ δὲ δοῦλοι αὐτῷ λέγουσιν· Θέλεις οὖν ἀπελθόντες συλλέξωμεν αὐτά;

records.literal_gloss: The but slaves to him say, Do you want then having gone away we should gather them?

en.L: And the slaves say to him, 'Do you want us, then, to go and gather them up?'
en.B: 'Shall we go out, then, and gather them up?' the servants asked.
en.R: The servants asked him, 'Do you want us to go and pull up the weeds?'

es.L: Y los esclavos le dicen: “¿Quieres, pues, que vayamos y la recojamos?”.
es.B: Los siervos le preguntaron: “¿Quieres entonces que vayamos a arrancarla?”.
es.R: Los siervos le preguntaron: “¿Quieres que vayamos a arrancar la mala hierba?”.

sw.L: Na watumwa wanamwambia, 'Je, unataka basi tuondoke tukayakusanye?'
sw.B: Watumishi wakamuuliza, 'Je, twende tukayaondoe basi?'
sw.R: Watumishi wakamuuliza, 'Unataka twende tukayang'oe magugu hayo?'

decisions.choice: do you want us to gather them?: a polite request for orders
decisions.reason: The slaves are ready to act at once and ask what their owner wishes.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: le dicen (L); le preguntaron (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps Matthew's present of narration; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the pretérito. The same in verse 29.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable (wakamuuliza)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps Matthew's present of narration; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past. The same in verse 29.

source.text: ὁ δέ φησιν· Οὔ, μήποτε συλλέγοντες τὰ ζιζάνια ἐκριζώσητε ἅμα αὐτοῖς τὸν σῖτον·

records.literal_gloss: He but says, No, lest gathering the weeds you uproot together with them the wheat;

en.L: But he says, 'No, lest while gathering the weeds you uproot the wheat along with them.
en.B: 'No,' he replied, 'for in gathering the weeds you might pull up the wheat with them.
en.R: 'No,' he answered. 'When you pull up the weeds, you might pull up some of the wheat with them.

es.L: Pero él dice: “No, no vaya a ser que, recogiendo la cizaña, {{plural_you:desarraiguen|desarraiguéis}} junto con ella el trigo.
es.B: “No —respondió—, porque al recoger la cizaña {{plural_you:podrían|podríais}} arrancar también el trigo.
es.R: “No —les contestó—. Si {{plural_you:arrancan|arrancáis}} la mala hierba, también {{plural_you:podrían|podríais}} arrancar parte del trigo.

sw.L: Lakini yeye anasema, 'Hapana, isije ikawa mnapokusanya magugu mkaing'oa ngano pamoja nayo.
sw.B: 'Hapana,' akajibu, 'kwa maana mnapoyakusanya magugu, mnaweza kuing'oa ngano pamoja nayo.
sw.R: 'Hapana,' akajibu. 'Mkiyang'oa magugu, mnaweza kung'oa pia baadhi ya ngano pamoja nayo.

decisions.choice: uprooting the wheat: the roots of the two plants are tangled together
alternatives: the slaves cannot tell the plants apart
decisions.reason: By now the plants can be told apart (13:26), but their roots have grown together in the soil.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the verbs addressed to the servants
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them, here and in verse 30, and for every plural "you" in the passage. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart.

source.text: ἄφετε συναυξάνεσθαι ἀμφότερα μέχρι τοῦ θερισμοῦ· καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ θερισμοῦ ἐρῶ τοῖς θερισταῖς· Συλλέξατε πρῶτον τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας πρὸς τὸ κατακαῦσαι αὐτά, τὸν δὲ σῖτον συναγάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην μου.

records.literal_gloss: Let grow together both until the harvest; and in time of the harvest I will say to the harvesters, Gather first the weeds and bind them into bundles in order to burn them, the but wheat gather into the barn of me.

en.L: Let both grow together until the harvest; and at the time of the harvest I will say to the harvesters, "Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn."'"
en.B: Leave them to grow side by side until the harvest. When harvest time comes, I will give the reapers their orders: "Pull out the weeds first, and tie them into bundles for burning. But store the wheat in my barn."'"
en.R: Let the wheat and the weeds grow together until harvest time. Then I will tell the workers, "First pull up the weeds and tie them together. They will be burned. Then bring the wheat into my barn."'"

es.L: {{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} que ambos crezcan juntos hasta la cosecha; y en el tiempo de la cosecha diré a los cosechadores: ‘{{plural_you:Recojan|Recoged}} primero la cizaña y {{plural_you:átenla|atadla}} en haces para quemarla, pero el trigo {{plural_you:júntenlo|juntadlo}} en mi granero’”».
es.B: {{plural_you:Déjenlos|Dejadlos}} crecer uno al lado del otro hasta la cosecha. Cuando llegue el tiempo de la cosecha, daré a los segadores esta orden: ‘{{plural_you:Arranquen|Arrancad}} primero la cizaña y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} con ella atados para quemarla. Pero el trigo {{plural_you:guárdenlo|guardadlo}} en mi granero’”».
es.R: {{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} que el trigo y la mala hierba crezcan juntos hasta el tiempo de la cosecha. Entonces les diré a los trabajadores: ‘Primero {{plural_you:arranquen|arrancad}} la mala hierba y {{plural_you:átenla|atadla}}. Se va a quemar. Después {{plural_you:lleven|llevad}} el trigo a mi granero’”».

sw.L: Viacheni vyote viwili vikue pamoja hadi mavuno; na wakati wa mavuno nitawaambia wavunaji, "Kwanza kusanyeni magugu na myafunge mafungu ili kuyateketeza, lakini ngano iingizeni katika ghala langu."'"
sw.B: Viacheni vikue bega kwa bega mpaka mavuno. Wakati wa mavuno utakapofika, nitawapa wavunaji maagizo: "Ng'oeni magugu kwanza, myafunge mafungu ya kuchomwa. Lakini ngano iwekeni ghalani kwangu."'"
sw.R: Acheni ngano na magugu vikue pamoja mpaka wakati wa mavuno. Kisha nitawaambia wafanyakazi, "Kwanza ng'oeni magugu na kuyafunga pamoja. Yatachomwa moto. Kisha ileteni ngano ghalani kwangu."'"

decisions.choice: bundles to burn: darnel was gathered and used as fuel
decisions.reason: Wood was scarce, and dried weeds were burned in ovens. The picture also points to judgment (3:12; 13:40-42).

decisions.choice: the harvest: a picture of God's final judgment
decisions.reason: John the Baptist used the same picture of wheat gathered and chaff burned (3:12). Jesus explains it in 13:39.

decisions.choice: reapers (B); workers (R); harvesters (L)
decisions.reason: The word means those who harvest. Balanced uses the traditional word for those who cut grain; Readable a plain one.

source.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔσπειρεν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Another parable he set before them saying, Like is the kingdom of the heavens to a grain of mustard, which having taken a man sowed in the field of him;

en.L: He put another parable before them, saying, "The kingdom of the heavens is like a grain of mustard, which a man took and sowed in his field;
en.B: He gave them another parable to think about: "Picture a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field. The kingdom of heaven is like that.
en.R: Jesus told them another parable. He said, "The kingdom of heaven is like a tiny mustard seed. A man planted it in his field.

es.L: Les presentó otra parábola, diciendo: «Parecido es el reino de los cielos a un grano de mostaza, el cual, tomándolo un hombre, lo sembró en su campo;
es.B: Les dio otra parábola para que reflexionaran: «{{plural_you:Imaginen|Imaginad}} una semilla de mostaza que alguien tomó y sembró en su campo. Así es el reino de los cielos.
es.R: Jesús les contó otra parábola. Les dijo: «El reino de los cielos es como una semilla de mostaza muy pequeña. Un hombre la sembró en su campo.

sw.L: Aliwawekea mfano mwingine, akisema, "Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama chembe ya haradali, ambayo mtu aliichukua akaipanda katika shamba lake;
sw.B: Aliwapa mfano mwingine wa kutafakari: "Fikirini mbegu ya haradali ambayo mtu aliichukua akaipanda shambani mwake. Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama hiyo.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia mfano mwingine. Akasema, "Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama mbegu ndogo sana ya haradali. Mtu mmoja aliipanda shambani mwake.

decisions.choice: a grain of mustard: a tiny seed of a garden plant that grows several feet tall
decisions.reason: The mustard seed was known for being very small (17:20). Black mustard grew in Galilee and could reach a man's height or more.

decisions.choice: the kingdom is like: like what happens to the seed in the story
decisions.reason: As in 13:24, the comparison is with the whole story: a small beginning and a great end.

decisions.choice: the picture first, then the comparison
alternatives: the kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed
decisions.reason: Balanced draws the picture first and then applies it to the kingdom, to keep the long sentence clear when read aloud.

decisions.choice: tiny
decisions.reason: Readable says why a mustard seed was chosen, as at Luke 13:19.

source.text: ὃ μικρότερον μέν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων, ὅταν δὲ αὐξηθῇ μεῖζον τῶν λαχάνων ἐστὶν καὶ γίνεται δένδρον, ὥστε ἐλθεῖν τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: which smaller indeed is of all the seeds, when but it is grown greater than the garden plants it is and becomes a tree, so that come the birds of the heaven and nest in the branches of it.

en.L: which is smaller than all the seeds, but when it has grown, it is greater than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches."
en.B: Of all the seeds it is the smallest, but once it is grown it stands taller than the other garden plants and turns into a tree, big enough for wild birds to come and nest among its branches."
en.R: It is the smallest seed that people plant. But when it grows, it is bigger than all the other plants in the garden. It becomes a tree. Birds come and make their nests in its branches."

es.L: que es más pequeña que todas las semillas, pero una vez crecida es más grande que las plantas del huerto y llega a ser un árbol, así que las aves del cielo vienen a anidar en sus ramas».
es.B: De todas las semillas es la más pequeña, pero cuando ya ha crecido sobrepasa a las demás plantas del huerto y se convierte en un árbol, tan grande que las aves silvestres vienen a hacer sus nidos entre sus ramas».
es.R: Es la semilla más pequeña que la gente siembra. Pero cuando crece, es más grande que todas las demás plantas del huerto. Se convierte en un árbol. Los pájaros vienen y hacen sus nidos en sus ramas».

sw.L: ambayo kweli ni ndogo zaidi ya mbegu zote, lakini inapokuwa imekua ni kubwa zaidi ya mimea ya bustani na kugeuka mti, hata ndege wa angani wanakuja kujenga viota katika matawi yake."
sw.B: Kati ya mbegu zote ndiyo iliyo ndogo kabisa, lakini ikishakomaa huipita mimea mingine ya bustani kwa urefu na kuwa mti, mkubwa kiasi kwamba ndege wa porini huja kujenga viota katikati ya matawi yake."
sw.R: Ni mbegu ndogo kuliko zote ambazo watu hupanda. Lakini inapokua, inakuwa kubwa kuliko mimea mingine yote ya bustani. Inakuwa mti. Ndege huja na kujenga viota vyao katika matawi yake."

decisions.choice: smaller than all the seeds: the smallest seed people knew to sow
alternatives: the smallest seed in the whole world
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the seeds his hearers planted, not of all plants. The mustard seed was the proverbial small thing.

decisions.choice: the birds nesting in its branches: a picture of a great kingdom that shelters many
decisions.reason: The prophets use this picture of a great kingdom (Ezekiel 17:23; 31:6; Daniel 4:12, 21). Some see the nations coming in; the parable does not say.

decisions.choice: a tree: a plant as big as a tree
decisions.reason: The mustard plant is not a tree, but it grows as large as one and has branches strong enough for birds.

decisions.choice: make their nests
decisions.reason: The verb means to settle or live in a shelter. Readable uses the simplest picture.

source.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.

records.literal_gloss: Another parable he spoke to them, Like is the kingdom of the heavens to leaven, which having taken a woman hid in of flour measures three until was leavened all.

en.L: He spoke another parable to them: "The kingdom of the heavens is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all [of it] was leavened."
en.B: He told them another parable: "The kingdom of heaven is like yeast. A woman took it and worked it into {{units:about 40 pounds|three measures}} of flour, until all the dough had risen."
en.R: Jesus told them another parable: "The kingdom of heaven is like yeast. A woman mixed a little yeast into a large amount of flour, {{units:about 40 pounds|three measures}}. Soon all the dough had risen."

es.L: Les dijo otra parábola: «Parecido es el reino de los cielos a la levadura que, tomándola una mujer, la escondió en tres medidas de harina hasta que fermentó toda [la masa]».
es.B: Les contó otra parábola: «El reino de los cielos es como la levadura. Una mujer la tomó y la mezcló con {{units:unos 18 kilos|tres medidas}} de harina, hasta que toda la masa subió».
es.R: Jesús les contó otra parábola: «El reino de los cielos es como la levadura. Una mujer mezcló un poco de levadura con mucha harina, {{units:unos 18 kilos|tres medidas}}. Pronto toda la masa había subido».

sw.L: Aliwaambia mfano mwingine: "Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama chachu, ambayo mwanamke aliichukua akaificha katika vipimo vitatu vya unga mpaka wote ukachachuka."
sw.B: Aliwaambia mfano mwingine: "Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama chachu. Mwanamke mmoja aliichukua akaichanganya na {{units:karibu kilo 18 za|vipimo vitatu vya}} unga, mpaka unga wote ukaumka."
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia mfano mwingine: "Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama chachu. Mwanamke mmoja alichanganya chachu kidogo na unga mwingi, {{units:karibu kilo 18|vipimo vitatu}}. Baada ya muda, unga wote ulikuwa umeumka."

decisions.choice: leaven: a lump of old, fermented dough kept back to make the next batch rise
decisions.reason: A little leaven works through a whole batch of dough. Elsewhere leaven pictures bad influence (16:6, 11-12); here it pictures the kingdom spreading through everything, for good.

decisions.choice: hid: mixed in, so that it could not be seen
decisions.reason: The word is unusual for mixing dough, and it fits the point: the kingdom is at work even when it is hidden (13:35, 44).

decisions.choice: three measures of flour: a very large amount, enough bread for a great many people
decisions.reason: A measure (saton) was a dry measure of perhaps 7 to 13 liters; the estimates vary. Sarah baked from three measures of flour for her three visitors (Genesis 18:6).

decisions.choice: yeast (B, R); leaven (L)
decisions.reason: "Leaven" is no longer an everyday word, as at Luke 13:21.

decisions.choice: about 40 pounds by default; "three measures" as the Measures alternative
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the unit, as at Luke 13:21. The size of a saton is uncertain, so the figure is approximate.

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 18 kilos|tres medidas}}
decisions.reason: Three measures were a very large amount of flour (meaning decision m3). Spanish gives a metric weight by default, where the English gives pounds, with the original measure as the alternative; Literal keeps "tres medidas".

decisions.choice: {{units:karibu kilo 18 za|vipimo vitatu vya}} (B); {{units:karibu kilo 18|vipimo vitatu}} (R)
decisions.reason: Three measures were a very large amount of flour (meaning decision m3). Swahili gives a metric weight by default, where the English gives pounds, with the original measure as the alternative; Literal keeps "vipimo vitatu". At Balanced the span takes in the linking word, which agrees with its noun ("kilo ... za", "vipimo ... vya").

source.text: Ταῦτα πάντα ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν παραβολαῖς τοῖς ὄχλοις, καὶ χωρὶς παραβολῆς οὐδὲν ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: These things all spoke the Jesus in parables to the crowds, and without a parable nothing he was speaking to them;

en.L: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables, and without a parable {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking nothing to them,
en.B: Everything Jesus said to the crowds {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said in parables; indeed, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them nothing at all without a parable.
en.R: Jesus used parables to teach all these things to the crowds. He always used parables when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them.

es.L: Todas estas cosas dijo Jesús a las multitudes en parábolas, y sin parábola nada les decía,
es.B: Todo lo que Jesús decía a las multitudes, lo decía en parábolas; de hecho, no les decía nada sin una parábola.
es.R: Jesús usaba parábolas para enseñar todas estas cosas a la gente. Siempre usaba parábolas cuando les enseñaba.

sw.L: Yesu aliyanena mambo haya yote kwa umati kwa mifano, na bila mfano hakusema nao lolote,
sw.B: Kila kitu ambacho Yesu aliwaambia umati wa watu alikisema kwa mifano; kwa kweli hakuwaambia jambo lolote bila mfano.
sw.R: Yesu alitumia mifano kuwafundisha watu mambo haya yote. Kila mara alipowafundisha, alitumia mifano.

decisions.choice: without a parable he was speaking nothing to them: his way of teaching the crowds at this time
alternatives: he never spoke plainly to anyone
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes his practice in this setting. He explained the parables to his disciples (13:36).

decisions.choice: a positive statement: He always used parables
alternatives: without a parable he said nothing
decisions.reason: The double negative is turned into a positive statement, which says the same thing more plainly.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span where Spanish leaves the subject unsaid
decisions.reason: The English marks "he". Spanish leaves the subject pronoun out ("les decía"), so there is nothing separate to capitalise; the setting goes on separate pronouns and possessives ("él", "su", "mi") through the passage.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on hakusema, hakuwaambia
decisions.reason: The English marks "he". Swahili carries it in the verb prefix, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives ("changu", "wake"), as in John. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English through the passage.

source.text: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου, ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ καταβολῆς.

records.literal_gloss: so that may be fulfilled the [thing] spoken through the prophet saying, I will open in parables the mouth of me, I will utter things having been hidden from foundation.

en.L: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "I will open {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from [the] foundation [of the world]."
en.B: This was so that the word spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled: "I will open {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth in parables; I will pour out what has been hidden since the world was founded."
en.R: This made what the prophet had said come true: "I will speak using parables. I will tell things that have been kept secret since God made the world."

es.L: a fin de que se cumpliera lo que fue dicho por medio del profeta, que dice: «Abriré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} boca en parábolas; proclamaré lo escondido desde [la] fundación [del mundo]».
es.B: Así se cumplió lo que había dicho el profeta: «Abriré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} boca en parábolas; derramaré lo que ha estado oculto desde que el mundo fue fundado».
es.R: Así se cumplió lo que había dicho el profeta: «Hablaré usando parábolas. Contaré cosas que han estado en secreto desde que Dios creó el mundo».

sw.L: ili kitimizwe kile kilichosemwa kupitia nabii, kisemacho, "Nitafungua kinywa {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} kwa mifano; nitamwaga mambo yaliyofichwa tangu kuwekwa misingi [ya ulimwengu]."
sw.B: Hivyo likatimia neno lililosemwa kupitia nabii: "Nitafungua kinywa {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} kwa mifano; nitayamwaga mambo yaliyofichwa tangu ulimwengu ulipoumbwa."
sw.R: Hivyo yakatimia maneno ya nabii aliyesema, "Nitasema kwa kutumia mifano. Nitaeleza mambo yaliyokuwa siri tangu Mungu alipoumba ulimwengu."

decisions.choice: Psalm 78:2: the psalmist's opening words, fulfilled in Jesus's parables
decisions.reason: Psalm 78 is a psalm of Asaph that retells Israel's history as a lesson. Its second verse promises to speak in a parable and to utter dark sayings from of old. Matthew sees the words come true in Jesus's teaching. The first line follows the Greek Old Testament; the second is closer to the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: through the prophet, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: through Isaiah the prophet, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, among them the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, read "through Isaiah the prophet", though the words come from Psalm 78:2. Early Christian writers already knew this reading. It may be original, and copyists removed the name because it seemed a mistake; or a copyist added Isaiah, the prophet Matthew names most. The Psalms were counted as prophecy, and Asaph is called a seer in 2 Chronicles 29:30. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: from the foundation, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: from the foundation of the world, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "of the world", the usual form of the phrase (25:34). Some early manuscripts lack it. Either way the sense is the beginning of the world. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a span on "my"
decisions.reason: The psalmist's words are fulfilled in Jesus, who speaks in parables, so the pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, as with the servant at 12:18.

decisions.choice: [of the world] (L); since the world was founded (B); since God made the world (R)
decisions.reason: "The foundation" alone does not say what was founded. All levels supply the world, which the phrase always means.

decisions.choice: I will speak using parables
alternatives: I will open my mouth in parables
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of the idiom and so has no pronoun for the speaker except "I".

source.text: Τότε ἀφεὶς τοὺς ὄχλους ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Then having left the crowds he went into the house.

en.L: Then, leaving the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into the house.
en.B: Then Jesus sent the crowds away and went into the house.
en.R: Then Jesus left the crowds and went into the house.

es.L: Entonces, dejando a las multitudes, entró en la casa.
es.B: Entonces Jesús despidió a las multitudes y entró en la casa.
es.R: Después Jesús dejó a la gente y entró en la casa.

sw.L: Kisha, akiwa ameuacha umati, aliingia nyumbani.
sw.B: Kisha Yesu aliuaga umati, akaenda ndani ya nyumba.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwaacha watu, akaingia ndani ya nyumba.

decisions.choice: leaving: sending away, dismissing
decisions.reason: The verb has many senses, among them to let go and to forgive. Here he leaves the crowds or sends them home.

decisions.choice: the house: the house of 13:1
decisions.reason: Jesus returns to the house he left at the start of the chapter.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

source.text: καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διασάφησον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν τῶν ζιζανίων τοῦ ἀγροῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And came to him the disciples of him saying, Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field."
en.B: His disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Tell us plainly what the parable of the weeds in the field means."
en.R: His followers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Please explain to us the parable about the weeds in the field."

es.L: Y se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, diciendo: «Acláranos la parábola de la cizaña del campo».
es.B: Sus discípulos se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y le dijeron: «Explícanos con claridad qué significa la parábola de la cizaña en el campo».
es.R: Sus discípulos se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y le dijeron: «Por favor, explícanos la parábola de la mala hierba en el campo».

sw.L: Na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakamjia, wakisema, "Tufafanulie mfano wa magugu ya shambani."
sw.B: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimjia, wakasema, "Tueleze waziwazi maana ya mfano wa magugu shambani."
sw.R: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimjia, wakasema, "Tafadhali tueleze mfano ule wa magugu shambani."

decisions.choice: explain: make clear, explain fully
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something plain.

decisions.choice: explain, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: tell, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read a more common verb meaning "tell" or "declare", as in 15:15. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ σπείρων τὸ καλὸν σπέρμα ἐστὶν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·

records.literal_gloss: He but answering said, The one sowing the good seed is the Son of the Man;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man;
en.B: He answered, "The sower of the good seed is the Son of Man.
en.R: Jesus answered, "The man who planted the good seed is the Son of Man.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, respondiendo, dijo: «El que siembra la semilla buena es el Hijo del Hombre;
es.B: Él respondió: «El sembrador de la buena semilla es el Hijo del Hombre.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «El hombre que sembró la buena semilla es el Hijo del Hombre.

sw.L: Naye, akijibu, alisema, "Anayepanda mbegu nzuri ni Mwana wa Adamu;
sw.B: Akawajibu, "Mpandaji wa mbegu nzuri ni Mwana wa Adamu.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Mtu aliyepanda mbegu nzuri ni Mwana wa Adamu.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's name for himself
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the title of himself (8:20; 12:40). The title recalls Daniel 7:13-14, where one like a son of man receives a kingdom.

decisions.choice: the one who sows: the one sowing now, as he speaks
alternatives: only at the end of time
decisions.reason: The present participle fits Jesus's work of sowing the word now (13:19).

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre
decisions.reason: The term-sheet title, recorded once in this passage: Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m1). It is a title and takes no gender setting.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The term-sheet title, recorded once in this passage: Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m1). It is never under the gender setting.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀγρός ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος· τὸ δὲ καλὸν σπέρμα, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας· τὰ δὲ ζιζάνιά εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ, ὁ δὲ ἐχθρὸς ὁ σπείρας αὐτά ἐστιν ὁ διάβολος· ὁ δὲ θερισμὸς συντέλεια αἰῶνός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ θερισταὶ ἄγγελοί εἰσιν.

records.literal_gloss: the and field is the world; the and good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; the and weeds are the sons of the evil one, \v 39 the and enemy the having sown them is the devil; the and harvest consummation of age is, the and harvesters angels are.

en.L: and the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the {{gender:children|sons}} of the kingdom; and the weeds are the {{gender:children|sons}} of the evil one, \v 39 and the enemy who sowed them is the devil; and the harvest is [the] end of [the] age, and the harvesters are angels.
en.B: The field is the world. The good seed stands for the people who belong to the kingdom, and the weeds for the people who belong to the evil one. \v 39 The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
en.R: The field is the world. The good seed is the people who belong to God's kingdom. The weeds are the people who belong to the evil one. \v 39 The enemy who planted the weeds is the devil. The harvest is the end of the world, and the workers who gather the harvest are angels.

es.L: y el campo es el mundo; y la buena semilla, estos son los hijos del reino; y la cizaña son los hijos del maligno, \v 39 y el enemigo que la sembró es el diablo; y la cosecha es [el] fin de [la] era, y los cosechadores son ángeles.
es.B: El campo es el mundo. La buena semilla representa a los que pertenecen al reino, y la cizaña, a los que pertenecen al maligno. \v 39 El enemigo que la sembró es el diablo. La cosecha es el fin de esta era, y los segadores son los ángeles.
es.R: El campo es el mundo. La buena semilla son las personas que pertenecen al reino de Dios. La mala hierba son las personas que pertenecen al maligno. \v 39 El enemigo que sembró la mala hierba es el diablo. La cosecha es el fin del mundo, y los trabajadores que recogen la cosecha son los ángeles.

sw.L: na shamba ni ulimwengu; na mbegu nzuri, hawa ni wana wa ufalme; na magugu ni wana wa yule mwovu, \v 39 na adui aliyeyapanda ni Ibilisi; na mavuno ni utimilifu wa zama, na wavunaji ni malaika.
sw.B: Shamba ni ulimwengu. Mbegu nzuri inawakilisha watu walio wa ufalme, na magugu yanawakilisha watu walio wa yule mwovu. \v 39 Adui aliyeyapanda ni Ibilisi. Mavuno ni mwisho wa zama hizi, na wavunaji ni malaika.
sw.R: Shamba ni ulimwengu. Mbegu nzuri ni watu walio wa ufalme wa Mungu. Magugu ni watu walio wa yule mwovu. \v 39 Adui aliyepanda magugu ni Ibilisi. Mavuno ni mwisho wa dunia, na wafanyakazi wanaovuna ni malaika.

decisions.choice: the world: the whole world of people, where the kingdom's seed is sown
decisions.reason: The field is wider than Israel or the church. Good and evil people live side by side in it until the end.

decisions.choice: sons of the kingdom, sons of the evil one: those who belong to the kingdom, those who belong to the evil one
alternatives: the people of Israel by birth
decisions.reason: "Sons of" names those who belong to something. In 8:12 "sons of the kingdom" are those who assumed a place by birth; here they are those who truly belong to it.

decisions.choice: the end of the age: the completion of this age, when God judges
alternatives: the end of a period of history
decisions.reason: The phrase is Matthew's (13:40, 49; 24:3; 28:20). It is the close of the present age and the start of the age to come.

decisions.choice: the devil: the slanderer, the evil one of 13:19
decisions.reason: The devil tempted Jesus (4:1-11). Here he is the enemy who works against the kingdom.

decisions.choice: the people who belong to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means. Literal keeps it with the gender setting, as at 8:12.

decisions.choice: the end of the world
decisions.reason: "The age" is not plain to young readers. Readable uses a familiar phrase for the same time.

decisions.choice: hijos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "sons" as the traditional alternative to "children". Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters, so the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: wana (no gender span); utimilifu wa zama (L)
decisions.reason: "Wana" already means sons and daughters, so the English choice between "children" and "sons" has nothing to change in Swahili. Literal says "utimilifu wa zama" (the completion of the age) for the Greek's word of completion (meaning decision m3); Balanced says "mwisho wa zama hizi".

source.text: ὥσπερ οὖν συλλέγεται τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ πυρὶ καίεται, οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος·

records.literal_gloss: Just as therefore are gathered the weeds and with fire are burned, so it will be in the consummation of the age;

en.L: Just as, then, the weeds are gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the end of the age.
en.B: The weeds are collected and burned up in the fire, and the end of the age will be like that.
en.R: The weeds are gathered and burned in the fire. That is what it will be like at the end of the world.

es.L: Así como, pues, se recoge la cizaña y se quema en el fuego, así será en el fin de la era.
es.B: La cizaña se recoge y se quema en el fuego, y así será también el fin de esta era.
es.R: La mala hierba se recoge y se quema en el fuego. Así será también al fin del mundo.

sw.L: Basi kama vile magugu yanavyokusanywa na kuteketezwa kwa moto, ndivyo itakavyokuwa katika utimilifu wa zama.
sw.B: Magugu hukusanywa na kuteketezwa motoni, na ndivyo mwisho wa zama hizi utakavyokuwa.
sw.R: Magugu hukusanywa na kuchomwa motoni. Ndivyo itakavyokuwa mwisho wa dunia.

decisions.choice: burned with fire: a picture of God's judgment on the wicked
alternatives: the weeds are only destroyed for fuel
decisions.reason: The burning of the weeds pictures what happens to evildoers at the judgment (3:10-12; 7:19).

decisions.choice: the end of the world
decisions.reason: As in 13:39.

source.text: ἀποστελεῖ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλέξουσιν ἐκ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα καὶ τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὴν ἀνομίαν, καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.

records.literal_gloss: Will send out the Son of the Man the angels of him, and they will gather out of the kingdom of him all the causes of stumbling and those doing the lawlessness, \v 42 and they will throw them into the furnace of the fire; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.

en.L: The Son of Man will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels, and they will gather out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom all the causes of stumbling and those who practice lawlessness, \v 42 and they will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
en.B: The Son of Man will send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels, who will collect from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom everything that leads people into sin and everyone who breaks God's law. \v 42 They will throw them into the burning furnace, and there people will weep and grind their teeth.
en.R: The Son of Man will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels. They will take out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom everything that makes people sin, and all the people who do evil. \v 42 The angels will throw them into the fire that burns like a furnace. There they will cry and grind their teeth.

es.L: Enviará el Hijo del Hombre a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ángeles, y estos sacarán de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reino todas las causas de tropiezo y a los que practican la iniquidad, \v 42 y los echarán en el horno del fuego; allí habrá llanto y rechinar de dientes.
es.B: El Hijo del Hombre enviará a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ángeles, que quitarán de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reino todo lo que lleva a la gente a pecar y a todos los que desobedecen la ley de Dios. \v 42 Los arrojarán al horno ardiente, y allí la gente llorará y rechinará los dientes.
es.R: El Hijo del Hombre enviará a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ángeles. Ellos sacarán de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reino todo lo que hace pecar a la gente, y a todas las personas que hacen el mal. \v 42 Los ángeles los arrojarán al fuego que arde como un horno. Allí llorarán y rechinarán los dientes.

sw.L: Mwana wa Adamu atawapeleka malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, nao wataondoa katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kila kinachosababisha watu kujikwaa pamoja na wale wanaoishi bila sheria, \v 42 kisha watawatupa ndani ya tanuru la moto; huko kutakuwa na kulia na kusaga meno.
sw.B: Mwana wa Adamu atawatuma malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, nao wataondoa kutoka katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kila kitu kinachowafanya watu watende dhambi, na kila mtu anayevunja sheria ya Mungu. \v 42 Watawatupa katika tanuru linalowaka moto, na huko watu watalia na kusaga meno.
sw.R: Mwana wa Adamu atawatuma malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Wataondoa katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kila kitu kinachowafanya watu watende dhambi, na watu wote wanaotenda maovu. \v 42 Malaika watawatupa katika moto unaowaka kama tanuru. Huko watalia na kusaga meno.

decisions.choice: causes of stumbling: whatever leads people to sin, and those who cause it
decisions.reason: The word means a trap or a stone to trip over. In Matthew it is what makes people fall into sin (18:7).

decisions.choice: the causes of stumbling and those who do lawlessness: perhaps Zephaniah 1:3
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Zephaniah 1:3 God says he will sweep away the stumbling blocks along with the wicked. Jesus's words may echo it.

decisions.choice: the furnace of fire: Daniel 3:6
decisions.reason: In Daniel those who would not bow to the king's statue were to be thrown into a blazing furnace. Here the furnace pictures God's judgment.

decisions.choice: weeping and gnashing of teeth: anguish and rage
decisions.reason: As at 8:12. Matthew repeats the phrase (13:50; 22:13; 24:51; 25:30).

decisions.choice: everyone who breaks God's law (B); the people who do evil (R)
decisions.reason: Lawlessness means living as if God's law did not apply (7:23). Balanced and Readable say it in plain words.

decisions.choice: people will weep and grind their teeth (B); they will cry and grind their teeth (R)
decisions.reason: As at 8:12.

source.text: Τότε οἱ δίκαιοι ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Then the righteous will shine out as the sun in the kingdom of the Father of them.

en.L: Then the righteous will shine out like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
en.B: In their Father's kingdom, then, the righteous will blaze out like the sun.
en.R: Then the people who do what God wants will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.

es.L: Entonces los justos brillarán como el sol en el reino del Padre de ellos.
es.B: Entonces, en el reino de su Padre, los justos brillarán con todo su esplendor, como el sol.
es.R: Entonces las personas que hacen lo que Dios quiere brillarán como el sol en el reino de su Padre.

sw.L: Wakati huo wenye haki watameremeta kama jua ndani ya ufalme wa Baba yao.
sw.B: Katika ufalme wa Baba yao, basi, wenye haki watang'aa kwa nguvu kama jua.
sw.R: Kisha watu wanaofanya mapenzi ya Mungu watang'aa kama jua katika ufalme wa Baba yao.

decisions.choice: the righteous will shine like the sun: Daniel 12:3
decisions.reason: Daniel says that at the resurrection the wise will shine like the brightness of the sky. The verb has a strengthening prefix: they will shine out.

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who do God's will
decisions.reason: In Matthew the righteous are those who live as God wants (5:20; 25:37, 46). They stand in contrast to the evildoers of 13:41.

decisions.choice: the people who do what God wants
decisions.reason: Readable says what "righteous" means here.

source.text: ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.

records.literal_gloss: The one having ears let him hear.

en.L: The one who has ears, let him hear.
en.B: Whoever has ears must listen.
en.R: If you can hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, pay attention to this!

es.L: El que tiene oídos, que oiga.
es.B: Quien tenga oídos, que escuche.
es.R: ¡Si {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}, {{plural_you:presten|prestad}} atención a esto!

sw.L: Aliye na masikio, na asikie.
sw.B: Yeyote aliye na masikio na asikilize.
sw.R: Kama mnaweza kunisikia, yasikilizeni haya kwa makini!

decisions.choice: whoever has ears, let him hear: a call to listen closely and take the saying to heart
decisions.reason: As at 11:15 and 13:9. Here the call follows a warning of judgment.

decisions.choice: ears, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: ears to hear, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: As at 13:9, many manuscripts read "ears to hear". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: If you can hear me, pay attention to this!
alternatives: The one who has ears, let him hear
decisions.reason: As at 11:15 and 13:9. The speech goes on, so no quotation mark closes here.
